Zones are rectangles in the yard frame used by the build scripts: s = metres along the pavilion's west facade from its NORTH end (south/street +), n = metres west of that facade (west wall +). costing.basis: Draft estimates from typical Budapest retail and second-hand prices; check before buying. Minimum = cash needed when everything that can be reclaimed, donated or bought second-hand is. Food for the workshop days is not included.

_more: A zone may list extra areas under 'more' (each with its own label, s and n); they share the workshop's number and colour.
_views: Camera per stage: az 0 = from the street side looking north, 90 = from over the west wall looking east, -90 = from over the pavilion looking west; el = degrees above horizon; dist in metres (x1.35 on portrait screens); focus = [s, n] aims at one area of a multi-area workshop.Chosen by ray-casting from each candidate camera to a grid on the zone floor and keeping the angle with no wall in the way; trees and roofs that still cross the line of sight are faded by the viewer. Midway tour stops and the stage views of W1-W6 were re-chosen (2026-10-14) with web/dev/camera_search.js: least blocked sight lines, no geometry within 1.5 m of the camera, never inside a building, closest to the previous framing.

phases.title: Ground murals
phases.hub: rollers on poles, brushes and trays from its kit; the paint waits in its store
phases.text: We paint two murals on the ground, designed together. Inside the street gate, on the asphalt, a grid of twelve 1.4 m tiles, each a ground colour with one shape over it, a quarter circle, a half circle or a triangle, in terracotta, ochre, deep green, slate, charcoal and off-white. The curves and diagonals run on from tile to tile, so the gate opens onto one composition rather than a row of pictures. At the other end of the yard, on the concrete apron in front of the raised platform, a smaller one in the same colours: six 1.5 m tiles carrying one ochre circle across four of them and a white peak pointing up the ramp, a floor for whatever happens in front of the platform. It is road paint: cars drive over the gate mural on their way to the bays, and both can be repainted, or redesigned, every year or two.
build: Road mural inside the gate, 4.3 × 5.9 m: 12 tiles of 1.4 m
Apron mural in front of the platform, 3.0 × 4.5 m: 6 tiles of 1.5 m
Water-based, non-slip road paint in six colours
Designed on paper first, then chalked out full size
skills: Setting out with string and chalk
Cutting in edges and rolling large areas

materials: Road paint 7 × 2.5 l: terracotta, ochre ×2, deep green, slate ×2, charcoal
Off-white: the bay lines' white, tinted
Concrete primer for the apron, 5 l
Masking tape, chalk line, string and pegs, a batten as a compass
Rollers on poles, brushes for the edges, trays
from the workshop space's kit, a few bought
Stiff brooms and degreaser to clean the asphalt and the concrete
cost.note: 39 m² of paint in all, 25 on the asphalt and 14 on the concrete. Road paint lasts a season or two: repainting it can become a yearly event.

phases.title: Window posters
phases.hub: its work tables carried out to colour in the pattern; brushes, paint and paste from the store
phases.text: We paint the yellow pattern of our concept onto the machinery house windows, all along the yard side. The pattern is drawn full size on paper, cut into pieces, and each of us colours in pieces at the work tables; the finished pieces are cut out and pasted onto the glass, upper and lower panes. Wheat paste washes off glass, so the windows can be redone for every season or event.
build: One yellow pattern across the machinery house's 15 window bays, upper and lower panes

Wheat paste: it comes off with water, so the pattern can change

Poster and acrylic paint, brushes, rollers, stencil card
bought / left over from the road mural (workshop 3)
Wheat paste (flour and water), sponges, a squeegee
A few large prints at a copy shop (optional)
cost.note: Pasted on the outside of the glass, so nothing is drilled or taped to the frames.

phases.text: Put the pallet beds on wheels, so the garden can follow the sun, gather around an event or make way for a delivery. Two hand pallet trucks lift each bed while the castors are slid under the pallet blocks and bolted on. Along the wall the beds are rolled apart into two quiet nooks, places to sit alone among the plants: a pallet bench bolted to each bed end and a rolling table between them. With the beds gone from the west wall, the three parking bays marked in workshop 1 come into use.

phases.text: Build garden furniture from milk crates and EUR pallets and set it out as an open-air cinema facing a patch of the west wall painted white: film nights, and a stage for readings, music and performances on the other evenings. Every seat has a backrest. Three curved rows: crate benches and crate chairs at the front, pallet benches in the middle, crate benches on a pallet riser at the back with the projector on a crate tower. The work tables, sawhorses and loose tools go back into the store to make room.

phases.title: Fire circle
phases.hub: the production line again: crate chairs and side tables made at the work table, boards cut on the sawhorses
phases.text: Milk crate chairs like the cinema's and small oiled pallet-wood side tables, set in a horseshoe around the yard's brick fire pit, open towards the pavilion. A tripod with a cauldron hangs over the pit: the day ends with a soup cooked together, and the circle stays a place for one person to tell a story and the others to listen. First the cinema furniture is stacked along the west wall under the screen, ready for the next film night, and the borrowed pallet truck goes back.

phases.title: Covered open space
phases.hub: the notice board cut and framed at the work table; the beer-tent set kept in the store
phases.text: Under the gabled shelter, a place to sit together, eat and talk out of the rain. Nothing is built for it: a beer-tent set (sörpad) comes out of the store, a folding table and two benches, and the fire circle's crate chairs and little side tables are carried over to make a low corner at the west end and a pair of seats by the new notice board. Everything folds or lifts, so it can go back to the store or to the fire pit for an evening.
